Report: EA's NHL 27 is using genAI to make commentator voiceover
Business
News
Report: EA is using genAI for commentator voiceover in NHL 27
Veteran sports commentator John Buccigross claims EA showed him the tech using his voice for in-game commentary in NHL 27.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 8, 2026
2 Min Read
Image via EA
Veteran spots commentator John Buccigross claims that EA Sports is using generative AI (genAI) to create voiceover for in-game commentary in professional hockey simulator
NHL 27
.
As reported by
IGN
(and
first spotted
by Insider Gaming executive editor Mike Straw), Buccigross told the
Chirpin Zebras podcast
about his participation in the game. This also led to him mentioning that EA is using genAI, as per an alleged demonstration.
"They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," Buccigross says on the podcast. "It's like 'wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it."
The commentator adds that sometimes "AI will get something wrong," referencing an example during the alleged presentation. At one point while playing back his AI voice, it said "Score! And the crowd gets out of the chairs!", to which Buccigross said that they're called seats instead.
Related:

"So, little things like that, you gotta go back and listen because words matter. [...] But then you can make AI smarter; in the future they'll say seats, they won't say chairs. You have to manually put that in. That was kind of a funny anecdote from the process," he says.
GenAI has garnered a
largely negative reception from developers
in recent years, with many arguing that it is having a corrosive effect on the industry. EA boss Andrew Wilson, on the other hand, has been adamant about his positive outlook on the tech. Back in 2024, he said that
60 percent of development processes
could be "impacted by generative AI," adding that the tech is one the publisher was "embracing deeply."
Later that year, he reinforced the sentiment to investors, claiming genAI is at the "
very core
" of EA's business and that it's far from a "buzzword." In late 2025,
EA partnered with Stability AI
to co-develop AI models, tools, and workflows, claiming that this would empower its development teams to "reimagine how content is built."
Buccigross might seemingly be okay with his voice being allegedly replicated by artificial intelligence, but it's unsure whether EA is using the tech in other aspects of the game as well.
Game Developer has contacted EA for clarification on the matter.
